prompt_version: s5-extract-facts-v2 (adapted from Paleo Atlas extract-facts-v3; v2 after Sofía's S5 review)

facts.statement: The research was a single-center cohort study that followed 23 people who had surgery to remove a low-grade brain tumor at a hospital in Germany.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Participants were tested before their operation, just before leaving the hospital, and again three months later using a set of standard tests.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The tests measured overall clinical status, mental abilities, physical movement, and the patients' own reports of their quality of life.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Walking speed and the ability to perform daily roles dropped at first but improved by the three-month check, while social interactions and bowel regularity got better.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: There were no significant changes over time in the scores for mental tests or general clinical health measures.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The size of the tumor, the swelling around it, or where it was located did not clearly predict how well patients' thinking skills would recover.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The authors note that bigger studies are required to confirm these results and to help doctors advise patients.
facts.subject: humans
